smith runs a monorepo in Node, Go, Python, Rust, .NET, Ruby, PHP, C++, Dart, the JVM and Bicep (and anything a plugin adds):
it scaffolds projects, runs their tasks in dependency order from a cache,
generates CI pipelines, and releases packages from conventional commits.

Usage:
  smith [command]

Examples:
  smith                      open the interactive menu (in a terminal)
  smith new acme
  smith add app web --lang node
  smith build

Create:
  add            Add an app, an internal lib or a publishable package
  adopt          Report what bringing an existing repository under smith involves, and take the steps
  config         Read and change settings of smith.toml
  convert        Convert an Nx workspace (or one made by the old mnci) to smith
  new            Create a monorepo: configuration, git, CI pipelines and a first commit
  remove         Remove a project: its directory, its traces in the workspace, its CI
  upgrade        Bring the workspace up to this smith and its recipes: migrate smith.toml, regenerate the files smith owns

Work:
  build          Run the build task (same as `smith run build`)
  dev            Start several projects together, such as a frontend and the API it calls
  install        Add packages to a project with its own toolchain, or install the whole workspace
  lint           Run the lint task (same as `smith run lint`)
  run            Run tasks on projects, in dependency order, from cache when nothing changed
  sync           Make every project declare a shared dependency at the same version
  test           Run the test task (same as `smith run test`)
  typecheck      Run the typecheck task (same as `smith run typecheck`)
  uninstall      Remove packages from a project with its own toolchain
  up             Show dependencies with newer releases and update the ones you pick

Ship:
  ci             Run a CI phase, or regenerate the pipelines
  pipeline       Add a ready-made pipeline: e2e, package-zip, deploy-pages, deploy-azure-function
  release        Version, publish and
